\caption{Classification controls in the primary symmetric-firm-effects design, 2018--2022 returns. FE denotes symmetric additive firm effects. The first two rows add pair-level matching indicators to the full panel; the third retains only pairs sharing an industry. Labels come from the undated sample-roster snapshot, so these are retrospective controls. Intervals are 95\% multinomial node-bootstrap percentile intervals. Full-panel rows reuse the main schedule; the within-industry row resamples its incident firms, retaining only within-industry edges. $\Delta D$/1 SD uses each row's distance standard deviation; $\Delta\rho$ translates that effect at the row's median chord distance using $\rho=1-D^2/2$ and is a fitted contrast. Partial $R^2$ is $1-\mathrm{SSE}_{\mathrm{full}}/\mathrm{SSE}_{\mathrm{restricted}}$, where the restricted model removes only $W_2$, retaining all controls. The within-industry row changes the sample and has a distinct baseline. The last two rows restrict the panel to firms covered by the Hoberg--Phillips ETNIC network and share one resampling schedule; ETNIC is the mean 10-K business-description similarity over the fiscal years of the return window.}
